summary: A GitHub issue (#3088) in the Npgsql repository, opened by OoLunar on July 28, 2020, reports that NpgsqlCommand.ExecuteNonQuery appeared to freeze with no output when a parameter of type Text was set to a ulong value. Maintainers roji and YohDeadfall tried to reproduce it; roji found the real cause was a type mismatch (Can't write CLR type System.Int64 with handler type TextHandler), which a ToString() on the value fixed. OoLunar closed the issue as completed, and a debugger stack trace later showed the exception, suggesting a try-catch elsewhere in the project (possibly Discord.NET) had hidden it.
one_line: GitHub issue in the Npgsql repo where ExecuteNonQuery seemed to hang, later traced to a Text parameter receiving a ulong value.
key_facts: GitHub issue #3088 in the npgsql/npgsql repository was opened by OoLunar on Jul 28, 2020 and titled 'ExecuteNonQuery freezes with no output in DEBUG output (Possibly due to syntax error?)'.
The issue was closed as completed by OoLunar on Jul 28, 2020.
OoLunar reported Npgsql version 4.1.4, PostgreSQL version 12.0, and operating systems Windows 10 (Client) and Debian 10 (Host).
The reported code froze at Command.ExecuteNonQuery() on a SELECT query with a parameter 'guildID' of type NpgsqlDbType.Text.
YohDeadfall suggested the table might have many records without an index or primary key, and recommended bigint instead of text for guild_id for performance reasons.
OoLunar stated the guild_id column had a UNIQUE constraint and the database was fresh with 1 record.
roji could not reproduce the freeze with a clean sample using a TEXT guild_id column and a ulong value converted with ToString().
roji reported that after cleaning up the sample, the error was "Can't write CLR type System.Int64 with handler type TextHandler" because the Text parameter was set to a ulong value.
roji stated that adding a ToString on the parameter value made the sample work, printing 466356954865074176, Here 1, and Here 2.
OoLunar said they had never received the type casting error and apologized for wasting time.
YohDeadfall asked whether a try-catch might hide the error and suggested stopping the debugger when the app hangs to show the stack trace.
After running the project through the VSC debugger, OoLunar reported that the exception showed clearly.
OoLunar suspected the project's use of Discord.NET might be catching errors and said the problem was no longer an Npgsql issue but a lack of debugging.
The issue had 3 participants: roji, YohDeadfall, and OoLunar.
